title-group.article-title: GSK343, an inhibitor of EZH2, prevents acquired cisplatin resistance in bladder cancer

abstract.p: Epigenetic alterations are emerging as a major driver of acquired cisplatin (CDDP) resistance in bladder cancer (BCa). The study investigated whether GSK343, an inhibitor of Enhancer of Zeste Homolog 2 (EZH2), can overcome CDDP resistance in BCa. CDDP-resistant T24 and 5637 cells were treated GSK343 (5, 10, or 20µM) for 48 h. Cell viability was assessed using CCK-8 assays, clonogenic survival using colony formation assays, migration capacity using wound healing (scratch) assays, invasion using Transwell assays, and apoptosis using flow cytometry. CDDP-resistant cells exhibited significantly higher EZH2 and H3K27me3 expression levels than parental T24 and 5637 cells. Treatment with 20 µM GSK343 markedly reduced EZH2 and H3K27me3 expression in resistant cells compared to vehicle control, with greater efficacy than lower concentrations (5 or 10 µM). Following 20 µM GSK343 treatment, resistant cells showed significantly reduced viability, fewer colonies, impaired migration, and decreased invasion compared to vehicle control. Furthermore, the apoptosis rate was significantly increased in resistant cells treated with 20 µM GSK343. The study demonstrates that GSK343 inhibits EZH2-mediated H3K27me3 and overcomes acquired CDDP resistance in BCa cells, suggesting its therapeutic potential for BCa patients with limited benefit from chemotherapy.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Bladder cancer (BCa) ranks second among globally diagnosed urogenital tract cancers and is associated with significant considerable morbidity and mortality if not treated optimally (Comperat et al. 2022; van Hoogstraten et al. 2023). BCa comprises two primary entities: non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) and muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) (Dyrskjot et al. 2023). Initial treatment for NMIBC involves transurethral resection; however, recurrence occurs in 50–80% of patients, 10–25% progressing to muscle-invasive disease (de Braud et al. 2002). For patients with MIBC, adjuvant cisplatin (CDDP)-based chemotherapy is strongly recommended following surgery due to its demonstrated improvement in disease-specific survival and overall survival (Alfred Witjes et al. 2024). However, the overall response rate to CDDP-based chemotherapy is only 40–50% in MIBC patients. Non-responders exhibited a 5-year survival rate of only 30–40% (Kolawa et al. 2023). Treatment failure due to acquired resistance to CDDP underscores the urgent need to develop alternative or combination therapeutic strategies to overcome this resistance (Wang et al. 2023).

Epigenetic modifications, including DNA methylation and histone methylation, are increasingly recognized as key drivers of acquired resistance to CDDP in BCa cells (Li et al. 2023). Enhancer of Zeste Homolog 2 (EZH2), the catalytic subunit of polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2), catalyzes trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 27 (H3K27me3). This modification transcriptionally silences target genes, including tumor suppressor genes, thereby promoting oncogenesis in various cancers including BCa (Kaur et al. 2024; Piunti et al. 2022). Over the past decade, numerous inhibitors targeting EZH2 methyltransferase activity have been developed and evaluated in preclinical models and clinical trials. Tazemetostat, recently FDA-approved for metastatic or advanced epithelioid sarcoma, is one such inhibitor (Duan et al. 2020; Liu and Yang 2023). The development and mechanisms of action of major EZH2 inhibitors are summarized in Table 1. Among these, GSK343 is a of S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM)-competitive inhibitor. Like others sharing a common pyridone indazole/indole scaffold, it competes with the cofactor SAM for binding to EZH2 and has been extensively studied for its anti-tumor efficacy in human cancers (Campolo et al. 2024; Zhang et al. 2025). Combining EZH2 inhibitors with CDDP represents a potential strategy to enhance therapeutic efficacy and overcome resistance mechanisms in various cancer types (Samarzija et al. 2022). For instance, GSK343 combined with gefitinib demonstrates enhanced inhibition of proliferation and growth in primary EGFR wild-type lung cancer cells (Gong et al. 2020). GSK343 has also been reported to sensitize human hepatocellular carcinoma cells to the multikinase inhibitor sorafenib (Liu et al. 2015). However, whether GSK343 can overcome acquired cisplatin resistance in BCa cells remains unknown. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the inhibitory effects of GSK343 on cisplatin resistance in BCa.

sec.title: Cell culture and EZH2 inhibitor
sec.p: Two human BCa cell lines, T24 and 5637 (ATCC, USA) underwent culture in 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS)-contained RPMI-1640 medium (Gibco, USA) under a humidified condition (95% air and 5% CO2. After exposure to gradually increasing doses of CDDP in 6 months, CDDP-resistant BCa cells were developed and designated as T24R and 5637R cells. GSK343 (S7164, Selleck Chemicals, USA) was resolubilized in 0.1% dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) (D8418, Sigma-Aldrich, USA) at a final concentration of 0–20 µM.

sec.title: Immunoblotting analysis
sec.p: The total protein was extracted from T24R and 5637R cells treated with vehicle control (0.1% DMSO) or GSK343 (5, 10, and 20 µM) for 48 h. After separation by using sodium dodecyl sulfate-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis, the protein was electroblotted onto polyvinylidene fluoride membrane (Millipore, USA). The membranes were overlaid with anti-EZH2 antibody (#36-6300, Invitrogen, USA), anti-H3K27me3 antibody (#9733, Cell Signaling Technology, USA), and anti-β-actin antibody (#4967, Cell Signaling Technology), followed by incubation with secondary anti-IgG antibody. The density of each target immunoblot was quantitatively normalized to β-actin.

sec.title: CCK-8 assay
sec.p: T24R and 5637R cells were seeded in the 96-well plate with 1.5 × 103 cells per well and treated with vehicle control (0.1% DMSO) or GSK343 (5, 10, and 20 µM). Each well was added with 100 µL CCK-8 solution (Transgen, Beijing, China) every 24 h until 72 h. After additional 2 h of incubation with CCK-8, quantitative detection of absorbance at 450 nm was performed to indicate cell viability.

sec.title: Colony formation assay
sec.p: T24R and 5637R cells following vehicle control (0.1% DMSO) or 20 µM GSK343 treatment for 48 h were seeded in 6-well plates (500 cells per well) and then harvested in 10% FBS-contained DMEM for 14 d. After adding 4% paraformaldehyde and crystal violet, colonies formed in the plate were imaged.

sec.title: Scratch wound healing assays
sec.p: Cell scratch assay was performed with T24R and 5637R cells following vehicle control (0.1% DMSO) or 20 µM GSK343 treatment for 48 h. Using a pipette tip, the cell monolayer was scratched to form an artificial wound gap. The wound gap healed after 24 h was recorded by using an inverted research microscope. The number of migrated cells into the would gap was calculated by using the Image J software.

sec.title: Cell invasion assays
sec.p: T24R and 5637R cells following vehicle control (0.1% DMSO) or 20 µM GSK343 treatment for 48 h were plated into the top portion of the 6.5-mm Transwell1 insert with 8 µM pore polycarbonate membrane (Corning, USA). The top portion of the insert was coated with Matrigel (1 mg/mL, 50 µL, Corning, USA). The bottom portion of the insert contained 10% FBS as a chemo-attractant. The inserts with invaded cells were then fixed in 3% paraformaldehyde and stained with crystal violet.

sec.title: Cell apoptosis assays
sec.p: T24R and 5637R cells following vehicle control (0.1% DMSO) or 20 µM GSK343 treatment for 48 h were seeded in the 6-well plate (1000 cells per well) and the apoptotic cells were examined by using the Annexin V-FITC/PI Apoptosis Detection Kit and the BD FACSCalibur flow cytometer (BD Biosciences).

sec.title: Statistical analysis
sec.p: Results of mean with standard deviation (s.d.) were summarized from three biological and technical replicates. The independent sample t test, One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) followed by multiple pairwise comparison, and two-way ANOVA followed by multiple pairwise comparison were employed in the statistical software of GraphPad Prism version 8.0 (GraphPad Software, La Jolla, CA, USA). Statistically significant difference was noted as a value of P < 0.05.

sec.title: GSK343 reduces H3K27me3 in CDDP-resistant BCa cells
sec.p: To investigate the association between EZH2 and CDDP resistance, we first analyzed protein expressions of EZH2 and H3K27me3 in resistant cells. The immunoblotting analysis showed that T24R and 5637R cells exhibited higher protein levels of EZH2 and H3K27me3 than parental T24 and 5637 cells (Fig. 1A, both P < 0.001). We next treated T24R and 5637R cells with vehicle control (0.1% DMSO) or GSK343 (5, 10, and 20 µM). The immunoblotting analysis revealed treatment with 20 µM GSK343 significantly reduced protein levels of EZH2 and H3K27me3 in T24R and 5637R cells but 5 µM or 10 µM did not (Fig. 1B, both P < 0.001). These data suggest GSK343 inhibits EZH2-mediated H3K27me3 in CDDP-resistant BCa cells.

caption.p: GSK343 reduced H3K27me3 in CDDP-resistant BCa cells. A, Immunoblotting analysis of EZH2 and H3K27me3 proteins in parental cells and CDDP-resistant cells. B, Immunoblotting analysis of EZH2 and H3K27me3 proteins in CDDP-resistant cells treated with vehicle control (0.1% DMSO) or GSK343 (5, 10, and 20 µM) for 48 h. Results were yielded from six independent experiments. Student’s t tests were performed for panel A and one-way ANOVA plus Tukey’s post-hoc test for panel B. *p < 0.05

sec.title: GSK343 suppresses proliferation of CDDP-resistant BCa cells
sec.p: We proceeded to evaluate the anti-proliferative of GSK343. CCK-8 assays showed significantly reduced viability in T24R and 5637R cells treated with 20 µM GSK343 versus vehicle or lower concentrations (5 and 10 µM) (Fig. 2A, both P < 0.001). Consistent with this, colony formation assays demonstrated markedly fewer colonies in resistant cells treated with 20 µM GSK343 compared to vehicle control (Fig. 2B, both P < 0.001). These data indicate that GSK343 suppresses proliferation of CDDP-resistant BCa cells.

caption.p: GSK343 suppresses proliferation CDDP-resistant BCa cells. A, CCK-8 assays of CDDP-resistant cells treated with vehicle control (0.1% DMSO) or GSK343 (5, 10, and 20 µM) for 24, 48, and 72 h. B, Colony formation assays of CDDP-resistant cells treated with vehicle control (0.1% DMSO) or 20 µM GSK343 for 48 h. Results were yielded from six independent experiments. Repeated measures ANOVA plus Sidak’s multiple comparisons test was performed for panel A and Student’s t tests were performed for panel B. *p < 0.05

sec.title: GSK343 inhibits migratory and invasive capacity of CDDP-resistant BCa cells
sec.p: Metastasis requires precisely coordinated basic cellular activities like cell migration-invasion in addition to cell proliferation. The inhibitory effects of GSK343 on the proliferation of CDDP-resistant BCa cells led us to analyze the effects of GSK343 on the motility of T24R and 5637R. Wound healing assays revealed significantly impaired migration in T24R and 5637R cells treated with 20 µM GSK343, evidenced by reduced scratch closure relative to vehicle control at 24 h (Fig. 3A, P = 0.002 and P = 0.004). Additionally, cell invasion assays demonstrated fewer T24R and 5637R cells invading through the Matrigel towards the greater content of chemoattractant when treated with 20 µM GSK343 than those treated with vehicle control (Fig. 3B, both P < 0.001). These results imply that GSK343 suppresses both migratory and invasive capacities of CDDP-resistant BCa cells.

caption.p: GSK343 inhibits migratory and invasive capacity of CDDP-resistant BCa cells. A, Cell scratch assays of CDDP-resistant cells treated with vehicle control (0.1% DMSO) or 20 µM GSK343 for 48 h. B, Cell invasion assays of CDDP-resistant cells treated with vehicle control (0.1% DMSO) or 20 µM GSK343 for 48 h. Results were yielded from six independent experiments and analyzed by Student’s t tests. *p < 0.05

sec.title: GSK343 induces apoptosis in CDDP-resistant BCa cells
sec.p: Cell apoptosis of CDDP-resistant BCa cells was assessed with flow cytometry analysis in T24R and 5637R treated with 20 µM GSK343 or vehicle control. Flow cytometry analysis found that 20 µM GSK343 treatment resulted in a notable increase in cell apoptosis compared to vehicle control (Fig. 4, both P < 0.001). A graphic abstract summarizing GSK343’s role in overcoming CDDP resistance in BCa cells is presented in Fig. 5.

caption.p: GSK343 induce apoptosis of CDDP-resistant BCa cells. The apoptosis of CDDP-resistant cells treated with vehicle control (0.1% DMSO) or 20 µM GSK343 for 48 h was analyzed by the flow cytometry. The apoptosis rate was yielded from six independent experiments and analyzed by Student’s t tests. *p < 0.05
A graphic abstract summarizing GSK343’s role in overcoming CDDP resistance in BCa cells

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: The development of SAM-competitive inhibitors represents a significant advance in establishing EZH2 inhibitors as safe therapeutic options for cancer treatment (Zhao et al. 2025). Herein, we analyzed the inhibitory effects of GSK343 on CDDP resistance in BCa. Our results demonstrated 20 µM GSK343 reduced the significantly elevated expressions of EZH2 and H3K27me3 observed in T24R and 5637R CDDP-resistant cells compared to their parental T24 and 5637 counterparts. More importantly, 20 µM GSK343 treatment markedly inhibited the growth of CDDP-resistant BCa cell and induced apoptosis. Therefore, we concluded that the EZH2 inhibitor GSK343 has the potential to enhance the therapeutic efficacy of CDDP in BCa exhibiting acquired resistance.

The oncogenic role of EZH2 in BCa primarily involves the following mechanisms. First, EZH2 promotes transcriptional silencing of tumor suppressor genes in a PRC2-dependent manner, which constitutes its fundamental mechanism of action (Huang et al. 2022). PRC2 comprises three core proteins, EZH2, SUZ12, and EED. The suppressor of variegation-enhancer of zeste-trithorax (SET) domain within EZH2 mediates the histone methyltransferase activity, facilitating BCa development and reducing BCa cell sensitivity to CDDP (Ren et al. 2023; Vantaku et al. 2020). Second, EZH2 acts as an antagonist of the lysine demethylase KDM6A, leading to dynamic regulation of H3K27 methylation (Ler et al. 2017). The EZH2 inhibitor GSK126 could counteract the metastatic effects resulting from KDM6A deficiency in BCa cells (Liu et al. 2021). Third, PRC2-independent mechanisms involve EZH2 cooperation with other epigenetic modifiers, such as DNA methyltransferases and histone deacetylases, resulting in additional gene silencing and and chromatin compaction at key developmental loci (Vallot et al. 2015). Forth, EZH2 is phosphorylated by Akt at Serine 21 and by CDK1 at Threonine 350, and these modifications reduce its methyltransferase activity while enhancing its oncogenic potential in BCa (Chen et al. 2010; Rehman et al. 2022).

Earlier work provides evidence of anti-tumor activity of EZH2 inhibitors (Chen et al. 2019; Ozgun et al. 2024). GSK343, used in this study, functions via SAM competition. As the universal methyl donor for methyltransferases, SAM is a common substrate, and SAM-competitive inhibitors represent a primary approach for targeting EZH2 due to their high selectivity. GSK343, as a representative SAM-competitive inhibitor, exhibits over 1000-fold selectivity against other histone methyltransferases and 60-fold selectivity over EZH1 (Yu et al. 2017). GSK343 induces apoptosis by upregulating cleaved Casp-3 and poly ADP-ribose polymerase (PARP) and promotes autophagic cell death by reducing p62 expression (Xiong et al. 2020). Furthermore, GSK343 inhibits the activation of canonical and non-canonical NF-κB pathways (involving IκBα) and reduces glioblastoma progression (Scuderi et al. 2022). Additionally, GSK343 promotes a shift from H3K27me3 to H3K27ac at the FOSB promoter, upregulating its expression and contributing to the suppression of triple-negative breast cancer (Zhang et al. 2020). Notably, germinal center B-cell-diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) cell lines developing acquired resistance to GSK343 differentiated toward an activated B-cell-DLBCL phenotype, suggesting the important role of EZH2 targeting in anti-cancer therapy (Preston et al. 2022). In the context of chronic kidney disease, GSK343 upregulates MST1 via EZH2 inhibition, suppressing YAP1 and promoting M2 macrophage polarization, thereby mitigating hypercalcemia-induced neural injuries (Cao et al. 2024). Given the anti-tumor effects of EZH2 inhibitors, combination therapies with CDDP are being actively investigated to overcome CDDP resistance (Samarzija et al. 2022). Gong et al. (Gong et al. 2020) reported GSK343 treatment reversed resistance to gefitinib in primary EGFR wild-type lung cancer cells, aligning with our results.

This study has several limitations. First, there is lack of group in which resistant cells were treated concurrently with CDDP and GSK343. Further investigations should be required to validate resistant cells regaining sensitivity to CDDP after GSK343 treatment. In addition, there is lack of in vivo model in this study. Animal studies or patient-derived xenografts are warranted to further assess the efficacy of GSK343 against CDDP resistance.

In conclusion, the study demonstrates that EZH2-meidated H3K27me3 represents as an epigenetic regulation mechanism potentially associated with acquired CDDP resistance in BCa. GSK343-mediated inhibition of EZH2, leading to reduced H3K27me3, could prevent acquired resistance to CDDP in BCa cells. Our findings broaden the understanding of incorporating EZH2 inhibitors into CDDP combination therapy to overcome acquired resistance to CDDP in BCa patients.
